| File | For |
|---|---|
| `TurboDL-Setup-0.5.0.exe` | Windows 10/11 (x64) |
| `TurboDL-0.5.0-arm64.dmg` | macOS on Apple Silicon (M1 and newer) |

## What's new

- **Instagram links:** add a post, reel, story or highlight link (Add URL or Ctrl+V), or right-click on Instagram → **Open in TurboDL**, and pick its photos and videos. Public posts and reels work without signing in.
- **Saved:** **Instagram → Saved** shows your saved posts and collections. Pick posts and press **Next**, or back up a whole collection into `Instagram/Saved/<collection>`. A later backup only saves what is new, and a stopped one continues where it stopped.
- **Profiles:** open a profile by link or username to see its posts (reels included) page by page. Pick posts, or back the profile up into `Instagram/<username>`. **Instagram → Profiles** lists the profiles you backed up.
- **Highlights:** on a profile, switch to **Highlights** to pick highlights and their stories, or back them all up into `Instagram/<username> · Highlights`.
- **Signing in:** sign in once on Instagram's own page inside TurboDL, or let the browser extension pass your browser's Instagram session. The session is stored encrypted.
- **Careful with your account:** TurboDL asks Instagram for one page at a time, leaves a pause between requests, and stops when Instagram asks it to slow down.
- Hold a picture in any Instagram grid to see it large.

## Updating

- Install the new version over the old one and open TurboDL once.
- Chromium browsers: copy the extension again with **Settings → Install the browser extension…** and press **reload (⟳)** on the TurboDL card on the browser's extensions page. The "Open in TurboDL" menu on Instagram comes with this version of the extension.
- Firefox: open `TurboDL-Firefox-0.5.0.xpi` in Firefox. Regular Firefox only installs add-ons signed by Mozilla; if this file is unsigned, use Firefox Developer Edition, Nightly or ESR with `xpinstall.signatures.required` set to `false`.

The apps are not signed: on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**; on macOS right-click TurboDL → **Open** the first time (or run `xattr -cr /Applications/TurboDL.app`).
